Their diet consists primarily of desert-dwelling small rodents (like gerbils and jerboas), birds, reptiles (such as venomous and non-venomous snakes and lizards), and arthropods.

Their prey includes aquatic invertebrates, small fish, crustaceans, and sometimes aquatic insects.

Because sand cats live in hyper-arid, terrestrial desert environments and eels live in aquatic or marine environments, their geographical ranges and ecological niches do not overlap. Therefore, sand cats do not interact with eels, nor do they encounter or actively avoid the aquatic prey of eels.
